new_statements.quote: STRESS falls on : 1) the last but one syllable of words ending with a vowel : lIbro book; tAblo table; pAtro father; mAtro mother; Almo soul; korAgo courage; ... 2) the last syllable of words ending with a consonant : amOr love; amIk friend; gardEn garden; kanOn gun; aventUr adventure; experimEnt experiment; mi amAr I love; vu venAr you come; zi vidOr they will see; vu venUr you would come. The s of the plural does not displace the stress : lIbros, tAblos, mAtros, serIos, amIkos, gardEnos, aventUros, experimEntos. [p.13] Letter y, being a consonant, cannot carry the stress ... Before another vowel, i always gets stress, even in words that already have another stress : folIo madness; mIopIo shortsightedness; bIologIo biology.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is final if the word ends in a consonant and penultimate if it ends in a vowel (i.e. a closed final syllable attracts stress, otherwise penult); the plural ending -s is ignored for stress (lIbros, gardEnos keep the singular's stress). Orthographic y is a consonant and never bears stress; i immediately before another vowel is always stressed (bIologIo, with more than one stress); u after a or e (kAuzo, nEutra, Auto) and u in guo/gu/ku+V (lInguo) is non-syllabic and never stressed. No written accent marks, except an accent or apostrophe on foreign/universal words ending in a stressed vowel (pasha', papa').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described as such; compounds carry 'two or more stresses, each component keeping its own stress' (dOrfoskOl, ArtIstor, IsnOn, nOnek nOnisnOn), and words with prevocalic i may have more than one stress (bIologIo).
new_statements.exceptions: Plural -s does not shift stress; y never stressed; prevocalic i always stressed; u in au/eu and in gu/ku/qu+vowel never stressed; foreign words with final stressed vowel marked with an accent/apostrophe (pasha', papa').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level rule stated by the language's designer (prescriptive norm) with citation forms and inflected verb forms (amAr, venAr, vidOr, venUr); compounds keep one stress per member. French original: Cours pratique de Neo (1961) p.23 and Méthode rapide de Neo (1965) pp.12-13 give the identical rule ('L'accent tonique se pose 1° sur la dernière syllabe des mots se terminant par une consonne; 2° sur l'avant-dernière syllabe des mots se terminant par une voyelle').
new_statements.identity_note: Constructed IAL (ISO 639-3 neu, glottocode neoa1234) designed by Arturo Alfandari; the sources are the designer's own prescriptive manuals (French original 1961/1965, English edition 1966), i.e. the norm of the language rather than a description of a speech community. All three editions state the same rule.

sources.note: pp.12-13 'L'ACCENT TONIQUE — TONAXENT. L'accent tonique se pose: 1) sur la dernière syllabe des mots se terminant par une consonne: amOr, amIk, kanOn.; 2) sur l'avant-dernière syllabe des mots se terminant par une voyelle'; plural -s does not displace it; y never accented; i before another vowel always accented (bIopsIo, bIografIo); u unaccented after another vowel and in gu/ku + vowel; compounds have two or more accents. scanned in ocr4/.
